questions.q: What problem does a Slurm job array solve for a hyperparameter sweep?
options: It automatically picks the best hyperparameters without running any trials
It lets the entire sweep be submitted as a single job with an index, instead of one sbatch call per trial
It merges all trials into a single GPU process to save memory
It disables logging for all trials to save disk space
questions.explain: A job array (#SBATCH --array=0-39) submits one Slurm job that spawns many indexed task instances, each accessible via $SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID, avoiding the need to submit each sweep trial as a separate sbatch call.

questions.q: What does $SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID provide inside a job array script?
options: The total number of GPUs available on the cluster
A unique index for each array element, usable to select a different config file or input per trial
The current fair-share priority of the submitting user
The git commit hash of the code being run
questions.explain: Each task in a job array gets a unique $SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID value, which the script can use (e.g. to index into an array of config files) to run a different trial per array element.

questions.q: For a multi-node, multi-GPU distributed training job, why must the Slurm resource request match what the training launcher (e.g. torch.distributed.run) expects?
options: Mismatches only cause a minor slowdown, never a failure
If they don't match, ranks may fail to find each other or sit idle waiting for processes that were never scheduled
Slurm automatically adjusts the launcher's settings to match its own allocation
The launcher ignores Slurm's resource allocation entirely
questions.explain: The Slurm allocation (--nodes, --ntasks-per-node, --gres) and the distributed launcher's own settings (--nnodes, --nproc_per_node) both describe the same topology; a mismatch between them causes ranks to fail to rendezvous or sit idle.

questions.q: What is the key difference between squeue and sacct?
options: squeue and sacct are two names for the exact same command
squeue shows the live queue (pending/running jobs); sacct shows completed job history including exit codes
sacct only works for job arrays, while squeue works for all jobs
squeue shows historical jobs; sacct shows only currently running jobs
questions.explain: squeue -u $USER shows a user's currently pending/running jobs. sacct queries completed/historical job records, including exit codes, which is the right tool for diagnosing why a job that's no longer in the live queue failed.

questions.q: What do the %A and %a tokens expand to in a Slurm --output path for a job array?
options: The researcher's username and the current date
The array job's overall job ID (%A) and the individual array task's ID (%a)
The GPU model and the node hostname
The git branch name and commit hash
questions.explain: %A expands to the array job's ID and %a to the specific array task ID, so each trial in a job array gets routed automatically to its own uniquely named log file.
